summary: Backend-only fix verification of the brute-force lockout bug + full regression. Added /app/backend/tests/test_auth_lockout.py (12 tests) and re-ran the whole suite against the public preview URL: 57 tests, 56 passed, 1 failed (the failure is the pre-existing CORS wildcard+credentials config issue, not the lockout fix). LOCKOUT FIX CONFIRMED: throwaway email locktest@skilltrace.gov.in returned 401 x5 then 429 on attempts 6,7,8,9 with ZERO 500s; a throwaway REAL account (registered via /api/auth/register) returned 429 even with the CORRECT password while locked; provider@skilltrace.gov.in logged in successfully (200) while another email was locked, proving per-email keying; after clearing login_attempts the locked account logged in again (200); all 4 seeded accounts obtain valid JWTs (3-segment token, correct role, no password_hash leak). login_attempts has both the `identifier` index and the TTL `expires_at` (expireAfterSeconds:0) index. Admin password hash verified as bcrypt $2b$12$. ML regression: all 4 /api/ml/* routes still pass (health+metrics, 4/4 classify cases, weak=high/strong=low risk, match-identity 401 unauth + duplicate detection). Phase 2 regression (trainee scoping, followups, employment verification token flow, analytics) all pass, including the previously failing TestAuth::test_brute_force_lockout_after_5_failures which now sees 401x5 -> 429.

minor.issue: STILL OPEN from iteration 1: allow_credentials=True with allow_origins from CORS_ORIGINS="*". Verified on localhost:8001 AND through the public URL that a POST /api/auth/login with Origin: https://evil.example.com returns `access-control-allow-origin: *` together with `access-control-allow-credentials: true` — browsers reject credentialed requests under a wildcard origin. Harmless today (Bearer-header auth) but blocks any future cookie auth. Set CORS_ORIGINS to the explicit preview/prod origins. Covered by TestLockoutInfra::test_cors_credentials_config (currently failing by design to document this).

STILL OPEN: get_current_user (server.py:72) falls back to a cookie named access_token, but login never calls set_cookie (only Cloudflare's __cf_bm appears). Playbook item 'httpOnly cookie set on login' is NOT satisfied — either set httpOnly/Secure/SameSite cookie or remove the dead fallback.

Minor: _register_failure re-sets locked_until on EVERY failure and the 429 response body/headers give no Retry-After or remaining-time hint. Also the counter never resets except via the 30-min TTL/success, so lockout effectively extends indefinitely while an attacker keeps trying (acceptable security-wise, but a legitimate user cannot see when it clears).

Informational: seed.py achieves admin-password idempotency by wiping the users collection (clear()) then insert_one, rather than an upsert/update of an existing admin. Works for the demo but destroys any user created after seeding (e.g. real registrations).

action_items: Replace CORS_ORIGINS="*" with explicit origins (or set allow_credentials=False) — only remaining assertion failure in the suite.
Set the httpOnly access_token cookie on login or delete the cookie fallback in get_current_user.
Optional: add Retry-After / remaining-lockout-seconds to the 429 response for UX.
critical_code_review_comments: Lockout implementation now correct: tz_aware=True motor client + tzinfo normalization in _check_lockout + email-only identifier + TTL index — verified end-to-end through the ingress.
server.py is still 850 lines; split into routers (auth/trainees/followups/employment/analytics/ml) before Phase 4.
ml/placement_risk.py still opens a synchronous pymongo client inside the async process at startup (blocks event loop).
POST /api/ml/match-identity still loads all trainees per request (to_list(100000)) — O(N) per call.

success_rate.backend: 98% (56/57; the single failure documents the CORS wildcard+credentials config, no functional endpoint failure)

Regression tests again created a TEST_ employment record and flipped a seeded followup to 'responded'. Environment RESET afterwards: `python seed.py` re-run and `db.login_attempts.deleteMany({})` executed — all 4 demo accounts confirmed logging in, no lockout state left.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Suite: /app/backend/tests (conftest.py + test_ml_routes.py + test_phase2_regression.py + NEW test_auth_lockout.py). Run `cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/ -v`. Only TestLockoutInfra::test_cors_credentials_config fails and it intentionally documents the wildcard-CORS+credentials config. IMPORTANT: test_auth_lockout locks locktest@skilltrace.gov.in for 15 min (harmless, non-existent user); if you re-run auth tests, clear state with mongosh test_database --eval 'db.login_attempts.deleteMany({})'. Never hammer the 4 demo accounts.
rca_of_the_issue: Original 500 was a naive-vs-aware datetime comparison in _check_lockout plus a proxy-fragmented composite identifier. Both fixes verified: AsyncIOMotorClient(..., tz_aware=True) (server.py:33), tzinfo normalization (server.py:174-176), identifier = email only (server.py:193), and db.py TTL/identifier indexes. Lockout now engages at exactly 5 failures through the public ingress and is scoped per email.
